title: The Teaching of Vimalakirti (Toh 176, Thurman trans.)
description: The Teaching of Vimalakirti (Vimalakirtinirdesa, Toh 176), translated from the Tibetan by Robert A. F. Thurman for 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha, the non-profit project translating the Tibetan Buddhist canon (Kangyur), with the Tibetan text and English translation. Thurman, a leading scholar of Tibetan Buddhism, first published his translation of this sutra in 1976. One of the most celebrated Mahayana scriptures, it centres on Vimalakirti, a wealthy lay bodhisattva of Vaishali who feigns illness so that the Buddha's disciples and bodhisattvas will visit him. In a series of dramatic encounters he outwits the great disciples, displays miraculous powers, and leads a discussion on non-duality, culminating in his famous 'thunderous silence' as the supreme teaching on the entrance into non-duality. It affirms that enlightenment can be realised in lay life and influenced Chan and Zen Buddhism.
